decisions.claim: B stated or implied that liquor has a higher tax than other things
decisions.reason: A's 'You mean X' construction in turn 5 presupposes B said or implied something about liquor's higher tax; this is a genuine E2 presupposition.

decisions.claim: B stated or implied that liquor has a higher tax than other goods
decisions.reason: Same claim as c1 with only a trivial paraphrase ('other goods' vs 'other things'); c1 is the more faithful quote.

decisions.claim: B attributed a position to A that A denied
decisions.reason: A's 'No, I didn't' in turn 7 presupposes B attributed a statement/position to A which A then denied; valid E2 presupposition.

decisions.claim: B is expected to know how high the tax on liquor is
decisions.reason: A asking 'How high is the tax?' is a question directed at B but does not establish B's knowledge; it only shows A expects B might answer, which is not an attribute of B.
decisions.counterexample: B could simply say 'I don't know' or redirect to another source.

decisions.claim: B provided an explanation about why the government taxes liquor
decisions.reason: A's question 'Why would the government want to tax liquor so much?' presupposes the government taxes liquor heavily but does not establish that B provided an explanation; it is A seeking one.
decisions.counterexample: B might not have answered yet or might have said 'I don't know why.'

decisions.claim: B gave an explanation that A understood to also apply to why people buy cigarettes at these shops
decisions.reason: A's 'That's why… isn't it?' in turn 11 presupposes B gave an explanation (likely about tax avoidance) that A now extends to cigarettes; genuine E2 presupposition of B's prior contribution.
